title: Valencia and Silver Slipper jobs with Eddie Miller and Sidney Arodin
summary: Hug's first cabaret job at the Valencia, then the Silver Slipper, with remarks on Sidney Arodin's clarinet.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition

blocks.x: I don't know of any other bands that he played with, Dick. The only time that I had ever played with Bill was at the Fern Dance Hall. After I left the Fern Dance Hall, I'd like to mention that I went to my first nightclub job, or cabaret they called it in the old days, was the Valencia on Bourbon Street. That was about 1927, I think. And I played with a little outfit there. I believe it was Hilton Lamar's brother, Jimmy Lamar, played alto sax. And Chink Martin's son, Chink Junior, played banjo. Buck Rogers played drums at one time with us. And then after Jimmy Lamar left, we got Eddie Miller. That was the first time I'd ever played with Eddie. Eddie played outdoor saxophone in those days. We started working at 11 o'clock at night. We got off about 6, 7 o'clock in the morning. I don't think Eddie Miller was ever on time. One time, he was quoting his wife at that time. He'd get to work about 12 o'clock at night. He always had some good excuse though why it was late. The boss never seen the mind. But even in those days, Eddie was playing great saxophone. He always had that nice tone, good ideas, good taste. It was really enjoyable working with that little combo. In fact, I followed a good piano player in there too. Speaking of piano players, I had a good man playing there. He's a very, very, very wonderful person. He comes up to the jazz club meeting sometimes. I know his name as well as I do. Where does he live? He's a barber. Across the river? I think so. Hal Maranto? Hal Maranto, yeah. He was playing piano there at the time. I followed him. In fact, I followed him on the job. And I worked at the Valencia there for quite a while. As I said before, we had, let's see, Jimmy and Eddie Miller and Chink Martin Jr. and Buck Rogers. I don't remember if Emmet Rogers played drums there or not. But I stayed on that job quite some time. And the next job that I can remember came at the old Slipper, the Silver Slipper with Abbie Brunas. Abbie was playing trumpet there. And Emmet Rogers was playing drums in that band. And Sidney Ayrton was playing clarinet. And in fact, Sidney and Eddie Miller were both playing in that band. Eddie was playing alto and Sidney was playing clarinet. And I'll tell you one thing, Sidney played a fine clarinet. Didn't read a note, but sure played great clarinet.
I wonder where he got his style. I can't imagine.

I can't imagine because he certainly played different than anybody that I'd ever heard. He didn't sound like rap. He didn't sound like anybody that I'd ever heard of. You hear other people that sound like him now. Yeah, that's right.

And Sidney never gets any credit for it. He never gets any credit for it. But he sure did play a nice tone. He had a good, beautiful, beautiful tone and wonderful ideas. Well you know he had wonderful ideas to write a tune like Blazy River.
